intent.raw_query: Japan family with kids, $4500, cherry blossom season 2026, 10 days from NYC

selected_hotel.name: Maruyama Park, Gion district, Kyoto Boutique Stay

experiences.name: Cherry Blossom Viewing in Maruyama Park
experiences.description: Experience hanami (flower viewing) under Kyoto's most famous weeping cherry tree in Maruyama Park. Join locals for a traditional picnic beneath the blossoms, enjoy street food stalls selling sakura mochi and dango, and witness the magical illumination of the trees at night. A perfect family-friendly cultural experience that captures the essence of Japanese spring.

experiences.name: Teamlab Borderless Digital Art Museum
experiences.description: Immerse your family in a breathtaking world of interactive digital art installations spread across multiple rooms. Children and adults alike will be mesmerized by the flowing light displays, interactive projections, and immersive environments. This world-renowned museum blends technology and art in a uniquely Japanese way and is one of the most memorable family experiences in the country.

experiences.name: Tsukiji Outer Market Food Tour
experiences.description: Explore the vibrant Tsukiji Outer Market with your family and sample some of Japan's finest street food. Taste fresh sushi, tamagoyaki (sweet rolled omelette), grilled scallops, matcha ice cream, and more. Vendors are family-friendly and the lively atmosphere gives an authentic glimpse into Tokyo's culinary culture. A guided walking food tour can be arranged for deeper insight.

experiences.name: Arashiyama Bamboo Grove and Monkey Park
experiences.description: Walk through the iconic towering bamboo groves of Arashiyama and then hike up to the Iwatayama Monkey Park where over 120 wild Japanese macaques roam freely. Kids will love feeding the monkeys from inside a viewing hut while enjoying panoramic views of Kyoto below. Combine with a visit to nearby Tenryu-ji Temple garden for a full day of nature and culture.

experiences.name: Hiroshima Peace Memorial and Miyajima Island Day Trip
experiences.description: Take a meaningful and educational day trip from Kyoto or Osaka to Hiroshima's Peace Memorial Museum and Park, followed by a short ferry ride to Miyajima Island. See the iconic floating torii gate of Itsukushima Shrine, encounter friendly wild deer roaming freely, and enjoy local Hiroshima-style okonomiyaki for lunch. This culturally rich experience blends history, spirituality, and natural beauty in one unforgettable day.
experiences.location: Hiroshima Peace Park & Miyajima Island, Hiroshima Prefecture

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Japan
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

hotel.name: Maruyama Park, Gion district, Kyoto Boutique Stay

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Clear customs, collect luggage, and take the airport limousine bus or train to Kyoto (approx. 75 min from Osaka Itami or 2.5 hrs from Kansai International). Budget tip: use IC card (Suica/ICOCA) for cheaper train fares.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check in to Boutique Stay in Maruyama Park, Gion district. After settling in, take a gentle stroll through Maruyama Park itself — Japan's most famous cherry blossom park. If blossoms are still present in mid-April, enjoy the iconic weeping cherry tree (shidarezakura). Entry to the park is FREE.
day_by_day.evening: Walk the stone-paved lanes of Ninenzaka and Sannenzaka (5-min walk from hotel) as the lanterns light up at dusk. Browse souvenir shops and soak in the historic atmosphere. Grab a budget dinner nearby.

meals.breakfast: Eat on the plane or grab onigiri (rice balls) at a convenience store (7-Eleven/FamilyMart) near the station for ¥150–200 each.
meals.lunch: Convenience store bento box or standing ramen near Kyoto Station for ¥600–900.
meals.dinner: Ramen or gyoza at a local Gion eatery — try Ippudo or a local shop near Shijo Street. Budget ¥800–1,200 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Purchase an ICOCA card at the airport or Kyoto Station (¥2,000 deposit + balance). This card works on all trains, buses, and convenience stores throughout the trip. Keep jet lag in mind — take it easy today.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Kiyomizudera Temple (15-min walk uphill from hotel) — one of Japan's most iconic temples with stunning views over Kyoto. Arrive early (by 8:00) to beat crowds. Admission: ¥500 per adult, children free or discounted. Walk the Otowa waterfall and make wishes at the three streams.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Fushimi Inari Taisha (20 min by bus/train from Gion-Shijo Station). Walk through thousands of iconic vermillion torii gates. The full hike takes 2–3 hours but even a 45-minute walk up to the first viewpoint is rewarding. Entry is FREE. Return to Gion area by late afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll through Gion's Hanamikoji Street at dusk — prime geisha-spotting territory. Watch for maiko (apprentice geisha) heading to appointments. Window-shop and enjoy the atmospheric lantern-lit streets. No cost to walk and explore.

meals.breakfast: Convenience store onigiri and green tea or stop at a local bakery near Maruyama Park for ¥300–500.
meals.lunch: Tofu cuisine set lunch (shojin ryori-lite) near Kiyomizudera — look for set menus around ¥900–1,200. Alternatively, grab street food: yatsuhashi (cinnamon rice cakes) for ¥200.
meals.dinner: Nishiki Market area — try kushikatsu (skewered fried foods) at a standing bar. Budget ¥1,000–1,500 per person including drinks.

day_by_day.notes: Wear comfortable walking shoes — both Kiyomizudera and Fushimi Inari involve significant uphill walking. Bring water. Fushimi Inari is especially beautiful in late afternoon golden light.

day_by_day.morning: Explore Arashiyama district (30 min by bus or Randen tram from central Kyoto). Visit the famous Bamboo Grove (FREE) first thing in the morning before crowds arrive. Walk through towering green bamboo — a magical, serene experience especially good for family photos.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Tenryuji Temple garden (¥500 garden entry, ¥300 extra for temple interior) — a UNESCO World Heritage garden with a beautiful pond reflecting the Arashiyama mountains. Then cross Togetsukyo Bridge and walk along the Oi River. If cherry blossoms are lingering, this is one of the most picturesque spots in Kyoto.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Gion area. Visit Nishiki Market ('Kyoto's Kitchen') before it closes — a narrow 400-meter covered market with over 100 stalls selling pickles, tofu, sweets, and street snacks. Perfect for grazing and trying local foods cheaply.

meals.breakfast: Grab breakfast at a Kyoto-style morning café — coffee and toast set (モーニング moringu) for ¥400–600.
meals.lunch: Arashiyama street food: yudofu (hot tofu) or soba noodles at a local restaurant near the bamboo grove. Budget ¥900–1,200.
meals.dinner: Nishiki Market grazing dinner — try dashimaki tamago (rolled omelette), pickled vegetables, and grilled skewers. Budget ¥800–1,200 total.

day_by_day.notes: Take the Randen (Keifuku) tram to Arashiyama for a charming, old-fashioned experience (¥250 one way). Alternatively, Bus 28 from Kyoto Station is slightly cheaper. Saturdays can be crowded — aim for the bamboo grove before 8:30 AM.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Nara (45 min by JR train from Kyoto, ¥720 one way). Visit Nara Park — home to over 1,200 free-roaming sacred deer. Children absolutely love feeding the deer (deer crackers sold for ¥200). Walk to Todai-ji Temple, housing Japan's largest bronze Buddha statue. Admission: ¥600 adults, ¥300 children.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Kasuga Taisha Shrine (FREE outer grounds, ¥500 for inner garden) — famous for its hundreds of bronze and stone lanterns. Walk the forested path lined with moss-covered stone lanterns. Then explore Naramachi, the old merchant district with traditional machiya townhouses — FREE to walk through.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Kyoto by early evening. Relax near Maruyama Park — if cherry blossoms are still present, the park hosts evening illuminations (hanami season) which are free to enjoy. Grab takeaway food and have a picnic under the trees.

meals.breakfast: Convenience store or hotel breakfast before departing for Nara.
meals.lunch: Kakinoha sushi (persimmon leaf sushi) — a Nara specialty. Look for set boxes around ¥1,000–1,300 near Kintetsu Nara Station.
meals.dinner: Convenience store bento picnic in Maruyama Park under the cherry blossoms, or grab takeaway ramen. Budget ¥600–900.

day_by_day.notes: Deer in Nara bow their heads when you bow to them — a delightful trick to show children! Keep food secured in bags as deer are notorious for nibbling snacks. The JR Pass is NOT needed for this day trip — pay individual fares.

day_by_day.morning: Explore the Golden Pavilion — Kinkakuji Temple (30 min by bus from Gion). One of Japan's most photographed landmarks, the gold-leaf-covered pavilion reflected in the mirror pond is breathtaking. Admission: ¥500 adults, ¥300 children. Arrive early to avoid tour groups.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk or take a short bus ride to Ryoanji Temple — home to Japan's most famous Zen rock garden. Admission: ¥600. Sit quietly and contemplate the 15 rocks arranged in raked gravel. Then visit nearby Ninnaji Temple (FREE outer grounds) with its beautiful late-blooming cherry trees (omuro zakura) — these may still be in bloom in mid-April!
day_by_day.evening: Head to Pontocho Alley — a narrow lantern-lit dining street parallel to the Kamo River. Browse the atmospheric restaurants. Enjoy a riverside stroll along the Kamo River where locals gather to relax on the banks. Free to walk and enjoy.

meals.breakfast: Local kissaten (traditional Japanese coffee shop) near Gion — morning set with coffee, toast, and egg for ¥500–700.
meals.lunch: Standing soba or udon near Kinkakuji — quick, filling, and cheap at ¥600–800.
meals.dinner: Pontocho area — look for restaurants with lunch/dinner set menus displayed outside. Ramen, yakitori, or izakaya sets for ¥1,200–1,800 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Bus Day Pass (¥700/day) is excellent value if you plan multiple bus rides — available at bus terminals and tourist information offices. Ninnaji's omuro cherry trees are a hidden gem that bloom 2 weeks later than standard cherry trees, making mid-April ideal timing.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Osaka (30 min by Hankyu or Keihan train, ¥400–500 one way). Visit Osaka Castle and its surrounding park (FREE to walk the grounds). The castle tower museum costs ¥600 but the exterior and park are stunning and free. Cherry blossoms may still linger in the castle park.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Dotonbori — Osaka's famous entertainment district. Walk the iconic Dotonbori canal promenade, see the giant Glico Running Man sign, and browse the vibrant street food scene. This is one of the best places in Japan for cheap, delicious street food. Visit Kuromon Ichiba Market ('Osaka's Kitchen') for fresh seafood snacks.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Shinsaibashi shopping arcade (covered, free to walk) and Amerikamura (American Village) — Osaka's quirky youth fashion district. Return to Kyoto by 20:00–21:00.

meals.breakfast: Convenience store in Kyoto before departing.
meals.lunch: Dotonbori street food feast: takoyaki (octopus balls) ¥500, kushikatsu ¥800, or okonomiyaki (savory pancake) ¥800–1,000. Budget ¥1,000–1,500 total grazing.
meals.dinner: Kuromon Market fresh seafood skewers and snacks, or a standing sushi bar in Dotonbori. Budget ¥1,200–1,800.

day_by_day.notes: Osaka is the street food capital of Japan — this is the best day to indulge in cheap, incredible food. 'Kuidaore' (eat until you drop) is Osaka's motto. Use Hankyu Railway from Kyoto-Kawaramachi Station to Osaka-Umeda for a budget-friendly connection.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Philosopher's Path (Tetsugaku no Michi) — a 2km canal-side walkway lined with hundreds of cherry trees (some late-blooming varieties may still have blossoms in mid-April). FREE to walk. Start at Nanzenji Temple end and walk north to Ginkakuji. The path is peaceful, beautiful, and perfect for families.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Ginkakuji (Silver Pavilion) at the north end of Philosopher's Path. Admission: ¥500 adults, ¥300 children. The moss garden and sand cone (kogetsudai) are unique and fascinating. Then explore Heian Jingu Shrine (FREE outer grounds) — a large vermillion shrine with an impressive torii gate.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Gion for a cultural evening. Visit Gion Corner (traditional arts performance venue) — tickets are ¥3,150 but offers a condensed introduction to tea ceremony, ikebana, gagaku, koto music, and maiko dance. Alternatively, enjoy a free evening stroll through illuminated Gion streets.

meals.breakfast: Tofu breakfast set at a local Kyoto restaurant near the hotel — a traditional Kyoto experience for ¥800–1,000.
meals.lunch: Café or noodle shop along Philosopher's Path — many small restaurants cater to walkers. Budget ¥900–1,200.
meals.dinner: Izakaya (Japanese pub) near Gion — order shared small plates (edamame, karaage, gyoza, yakitori) and beer/tea. Budget ¥1,500–2,000 per person for a fun, social meal.

day_by_day.notes: Philosopher's Path is best experienced slowly — bring a camera. The path was named after philosopher Nishida Kitaro who walked it daily. For families, the canal has koi fish that children enjoy watching. Late-blooming sakura varieties (yaezakura) along this path often bloom into late April.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Sanjusangendo Temple (10-min bus ride from Gion) — home to 1,001 life-size golden warrior statues, one of Japan's most awe-inspiring sights. Admission: ¥600 adults, ¥300 children. Photography inside is not permitted, making it a pure, immersive experience. Allow 45–60 minutes.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Kyoto National Museum (adjacent to Sanjusangendo) — permanent collection admission ¥700, special exhibitions vary. The museum houses exceptional Japanese art, ceramics, and cultural artifacts. Then walk to Tofukuji Temple (15-min walk) — famous for its Zen garden and maple trees. Admission: ¥500 for the garden.
day_by_day.evening: Relaxed evening near the hotel. Visit a neighborhood sento (public bathhouse) for an authentic local experience — typically ¥500–800 per person. Then grab dinner at a local spot. This is a great evening to try kaiseki-lite (simplified traditional Kyoto cuisine) at a lunch-box shop (obento).

meals.breakfast: Convenience store or hotel breakfast — stock up on snacks for the day.
meals.lunch: Obento (bento box) from a local Kyoto deli or department store basement food hall (depachika) — beautiful, filling, and around ¥800–1,200.
meals.dinner: Local neighborhood restaurant near Maruyama Park — try Kyoto-style obanzai (small vegetable and tofu dishes). Budget ¥1,000–1,500.

day_by_day.notes: Sanjusangendo's 1,001 statues are genuinely breathtaking — even young children tend to be awed into silence. The museum is a good rainy-day backup option. Check the sento (public bath) etiquette before visiting: tattoos may not be permitted, and bathing is done before entering the communal bath.

day_by_day.morning: Half-day trip to Uji (30 min by JR Nara Line from Kyoto, ¥240 one way) — a charming small city famous for matcha green tea and the Byodoin Temple. Visit Byodoin Temple (¥600 adults, ¥300 children) — the image on Japan's 10-yen coin. Stroll through the beautiful garden and Phoenix Hall.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Kyoto and visit Nishiki Market one final time for souvenir shopping — local pickles, matcha sweets, and food gifts are excellent budget-friendly souvenirs. Then visit Kyoto Handicraft Center (FREE to browse) near Heian Jingu for traditional crafts. Alternatively, try a matcha experience at a local tea house in Gion (¥500–800 for tea and wagashi sweet).
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner in Gion — treat yourself slightly more than usual. Look for a set dinner menu at a mid-range restaurant. Many Gion restaurants offer kaiseki-inspired set menus at lunch prices in the evening. Alternatively, enjoy a final hanami picnic in Maruyama Park.

meals.breakfast: Matcha soft cream and green tea from a Uji street stall — a delicious way to start the day in Japan's tea capital (¥300–500).
meals.lunch: Uji matcha soba noodles — a local specialty unique to this region. Budget ¥900–1,200 at a riverside restaurant.
meals.dinner: Splurge slightly for a farewell meal — a Kyoto-style set dinner (teishoku) at a local restaurant for ¥2,000–3,000 per person, or a conveyor belt sushi (kaiten-zushi) for ¥1,500–2,000.

day_by_day.notes: Uji is a lovely, quieter alternative to crowded Kyoto attractions. The town is walkable and very family-friendly. Buy matcha products here — they are fresher and often cheaper than in Kyoto tourist shops. Uji Bridge is one of Japan's oldest bridges and great for photos.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Kyoto. Revisit Maruyama Park one last time for a peaceful morning walk — appreciate the park that has been your neighborhood for 10 days. Visit any missed shrines or shops near the hotel. Pack and check out (most hotels allow luggage storage after checkout).
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Kyoto Station area — browse the Kyoto Station building itself (a stunning modern architectural landmark with free rooftop observation deck). Shop for last-minute omiyage (souvenirs) at the station's many shops. Isetan department store in the station has an excellent basement food hall. Head to airport based on departure time.
day_by_day.evening: Departure — travel to airport. Reflect on an incredible 10-day budget journey through Japan's cultural heartland, cherry blossoms, and family memories.

meals.breakfast: Final Japanese breakfast — convenience store onigiri, tamagoyaki (rolled egg), and green tea. Simple, cheap, and delicious (¥400–600).
meals.lunch: Kyoto Station Ramen Koji (Ramen Street) — a collection of famous ramen shops from across Japan in the station basement. Budget ¥900–1,200.
meals.dinner: Airport dining or in-flight meal.

day_by_day.notes: Keep ¥3,000–5,000 in cash for airport transport and any final purchases. Return your IC card (ICOCA/Suica) at the station for a ¥500 deposit refund minus a ¥220 handling fee — worth doing if balance is low. Kyoto Station coin lockers (¥400–700/day) are perfect for storing luggage on your final day of sightseeing.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival & Transfer — Flight LH lands at 13:00, so no morning activities. Clear customs, collect luggage, and take the Haruka Express from Kansai/Itami Airport to Kyoto Station (~75 min), then taxi or bus to your boutique stay in Maruyama Park, Gion district. Check in and freshen up.
day_by_day.afternoon: First Impressions of Gion & Maruyama Park — After settling in, take a gentle stroll through Maruyama Park to see the iconic weeping cherry tree (Gion Shidare-zakura). Mid-April is peak or late bloom season — soak in the hanami atmosphere, grab a spot under the blossoms, and watch locals picnicking. Walk the stone-paved lanes of Hanamikoji Street in Gion and spot maiko (apprentice geisha) heading to evening engagements.
day_by_day.evening: Yasaka Shrine Night Visit — The shrine at the eastern edge of Maruyama Park is beautifully lit at night during cherry blossom season. Stroll through the lantern-lined pathways for a magical first evening in Kyoto.

meals.breakfast: Eat on the plane or grab a bento box at the airport convenience store (7-Eleven or Lawson) — excellent quality and budget-friendly (~¥500–¥800).
meals.lunch: Pick up onigiri, sandwiches, or a hot meal at a Kyoto Station convenience store or the underground Porta food hall before heading to the hotel (~¥800–¥1,200).
meals.dinner: Omen Kodai-ji — a beloved local noodle restaurant near Maruyama Park serving hearty udon with seasonal vegetables. Cozy, family-friendly, mid-range (~¥1,200–¥1,800 per person).

day_by_day.notes: Currency: Exchange yen at the airport for the best rates or use a 7-Bank ATM at 7-Eleven. Purchase an IC card (Suica or ICOCA) at Kyoto Station for seamless transit. April 15 is typically peak cherry blossom season in Kyoto — the park will be beautifully in bloom.

day_by_day.morning: Cherry Blossom Viewing in Maruyama Park (Featured Experience) — Rise early (7:00–8:00 AM) to enjoy the famous weeping cherry tree before the crowds arrive. The morning light is spectacular for photos. Pack a picnic blanket and enjoy a traditional hanami breakfast under the blossoms. Explore the full park, including the pond and smaller sakura trees.
day_by_day.afternoon: Kiyomizudera Temple & Higashiyama District — Walk 15 minutes uphill from Maruyama Park to the iconic Kiyomizudera Temple, a UNESCO World Heritage Site with sweeping views over Kyoto framed by cherry blossoms. Descend through the charming Sannenzaka and Ninenzaka stone-paved lanes lined with craft shops, matcha cafés, and souvenir stalls — perfect for families.
day_by_day.evening: Gion Corner Cultural Show — Book tickets for the Gion Corner performance (7:00 PM, ~¥3,150/adult, children discounted), a 50-minute showcase of seven traditional Japanese arts including tea ceremony, ikebana, koto music, and Kyomai dance. A wonderful cultural introduction for the whole family.

meals.breakfast: Grab fresh-baked pastries and coffee from Café de 505 near Gion, or pick up a traditional Japanese breakfast set (tamagoyaki, miso soup, rice) from a nearby kissaten (coffee shop) (~¥600–¥900).
meals.lunch: Kasagi-ya — a historic sweet shop on Ninenzaka serving matcha desserts and light snacks. Pair with street food like yatsuhashi (cinnamon rice crackers) from stalls along the lane (~¥800–¥1,200).
meals.dinner: Tousuiro — a tofu-specialty kaiseki-style restaurant near Maruyama Park offering beautifully presented, family-friendly multi-course meals highlighting Kyoto's famous kyo-ryori cuisine (~¥2,500–¥4,000 per person).

day_by_day.notes: Kiyomizudera charges an entrance fee (~¥500/adult, ~¥200/child). Wear comfortable walking shoes — the Higashiyama route involves cobblestone hills. Book Gion Corner tickets in advance online to guarantee seats.

day_by_day.morning: Fushimi Inari Taisha — Take the JR Nara Line from Kyoto Station (10 min) to Fushimi Inari Station. Hike through the iconic thousands of vermilion torii gates winding up the sacred mountain. Start early (8:00 AM) to beat crowds — the lower gates are manageable for all ages; adventurous families can hike to the upper viewpoints (~2 hours round trip to the summit).
day_by_day.afternoon: Nishiki Market ('Kyoto's Kitchen') — Return to central Kyoto and explore the 400-meter covered Nishiki Market, packed with 100+ stalls selling pickled vegetables, fresh tofu, grilled skewers, tamagoyaki, and unique Kyoto specialties. A fantastic sensory experience for families. Afterwards, browse Teramachi and Shinkyogoku covered shopping arcades nearby.
day_by_day.evening: Pontocho Alley — Stroll through this narrow atmospheric lantern-lit alley running parallel to the Kamo River, lined with restaurants and bars. In April, many restaurants open their kawayuka (riverside terraces) over the Kamo River — a quintessential Kyoto experience.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast if included, or stop at a local bakery or konbini near Gion (~¥400–¥700).
meals.lunch: Graze through Nishiki Market — try grilled skewers, fresh yuba (tofu skin), pickled vegetables, and tamagoyaki on a stick. Budget ~¥1,000–¥1,500 for a satisfying market lunch.
meals.dinner: Pontocho restaurant of choice — look for mid-range izakayas or ramen shops. Recommended: Kichi Kichi Omurice (book ahead — famous for theatrical omurice preparation) or a riverside kaiseki set menu (~¥2,000–¥3,500 per person).

day_by_day.notes: Fushimi Inari is free to enter and open 24 hours. Saturday will be busy — arriving before 8:30 AM is strongly recommended. Nishiki Market is best visited before 5 PM when most stalls close. Pontocho dining is popular on weekends; make reservations for sit-down restaurants.

day_by_day.morning: Arashiyama Bamboo Grove & Tenryuji Temple (Featured Experience) — Take the JR Sagano Line to Saga-Arashiyama Station (~25 min from Kyoto). Walk through the towering bamboo grove (free, open always) in the cool morning air — magical with filtered light. Visit adjacent Tenryuji Temple (~¥500) and its stunning Sogenchi Garden, a UNESCO World Heritage garden with cherry blossoms reflected in the pond.
day_by_day.afternoon: Iwatayama Monkey Park (Featured Experience) — Hike 20 minutes up a forested hillside to the Iwatayama Monkey Park (~¥550/adult, ~¥250/child) where 120+ wild Japanese macaques roam freely. Children can feed the monkeys through a wire mesh from inside a feeding hut — a huge hit with families. Enjoy panoramic views of Kyoto from the summit. Explore Arashiyama's riverside Togetsukyo Bridge area and rent a rowboat on the Oi River.
day_by_day.evening: Arashiyama Onsen & Return — Visit Arashiyama Onsen foot bath along the riverside (free public foot bath near the bridge) to soak tired feet before heading back to Kyoto. Return to Gion for a relaxed evening.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at your hotel or a quick stop at Saga-Arashiyama Station's convenience area (~¥500–¥800).
meals.lunch: Yoshida-ya — a charming riverside restaurant in Arashiyama serving tofu dishes and seasonal bento boxes with views of the Oi River (~¥1,500–¥2,500 per person). Alternatively, grab yudofu (hot tofu) from one of many riverside stalls.
meals.dinner: Back in Gion — Gion Kappa, a casual izakaya serving yakitori, karaage, and seasonal dishes in a relaxed atmosphere. Great for families (~¥1,500–¥2,500 per person).

day_by_day.notes: Arashiyama is very popular on Sundays — arrive by 8:30–9:00 AM for the bamboo grove. The monkey park hike is moderately steep; bring water and wear sturdy shoes. Children under 3 are free at the monkey park. The Sagano Romantic Train (Torokko) runs through the scenic Hozu River gorge — consider booking a round trip (~¥880/adult) if time allows.

day_by_day.morning: Nijo Castle & Kyoto Imperial Palace Park — Visit Nijo Castle (~¥1,030/adult, ~¥350/child), the shogun's former Kyoto residence with its famous 'nightingale floors' that squeak to detect intruders — fascinating for kids. The castle gardens are beautifully landscaped with cherry trees. Walk 15 minutes to the vast Kyoto Imperial Palace Park, a sprawling green space perfect for a family picnic under remaining cherry blossoms.
day_by_day.afternoon: Kyoto Railway Museum (Family Activity) — A 20-minute bus ride brings you to this excellent family-friendly museum (~¥1,200/adult, ~¥500/child) featuring 53 real locomotives including steam engines and Shinkansen. Kids can ride a steam locomotive around the museum grounds. Interactive exhibits on railway history are engaging for all ages — a fantastic balance of culture and fun.
day_by_day.evening: Kyoto Tower & Kyoto Station Area — Head to Kyoto Station's striking futuristic building. Ride to the Kyoto Tower observation deck (~¥900/adult, ~¥400/child) for panoramic city views at dusk. Browse the Isetan department store basement (depachika) for gourmet Japanese snacks and sweets to take back to the hotel.

meals.breakfast: Morning set at a local kissaten (Japanese coffee shop) near Gion — toast, egg, and coffee for ~¥600–¥900, or hotel breakfast.
meals.lunch: Picnic in Kyoto Imperial Palace Park — pick up bento boxes from a nearby convenience store or Nishiki Market leftovers (~¥800–¥1,200).
meals.dinner: Kyoto Station's Ramen Koji on the 10th floor — a dedicated ramen village featuring 8 famous ramen shops from across Japan. Fun, casual, and great value (~¥900–¥1,400 per person). Perfect for families who want variety.

day_by_day.notes: Nijo Castle requires advance booking on busy days — check the official website. The Kyoto Railway Museum is closed on Wednesdays. Kyoto Tower is open until 9 PM. Monday is generally less crowded at major attractions compared to weekends.

day_by_day.morning: Day Trip: Hiroshima Peace Memorial Museum (Featured Experience) — Take the Shinkansen Hikari from Kyoto Station to Hiroshima (~1 hr 45 min, ~¥11,000 round trip with JR Pass or individual tickets). Visit the Hiroshima Peace Memorial Museum (~¥200/adult, free for children under 18) — a deeply moving and important educational experience. Walk through Peace Memorial Park, see the A-Bomb Dome, and ring the Children's Peace Monument bell.
day_by_day.afternoon: Miyajima Island (Featured Experience) — Take a 10-minute JR ferry from Hiroshima Port (covered by JR Pass) to Miyajima Island. See the iconic floating torii gate of Itsukushima Shrine (~¥300 entry) rising from the sea — one of Japan's most photographed views. Walk along the island's waterfront, interact with the friendly wild deer that roam freely, and explore the vermilion shrine buildings.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Kyoto — Take the ferry back and Shinkansen to Kyoto, arriving by 7:00–8:00 PM. Enjoy a quiet dinner near your hotel.

meals.breakfast: Early konbini breakfast before departing (~¥400–¥700) — depart Kyoto by 8:00 AM to maximize time.
meals.lunch: Miyajima specialty: Anago-meshi (grilled saltwater eel over rice) — a local delicacy. Recommended: Fujitaya restaurant near the ferry terminal (~¥2,000–¥2,500 per person). Also try momiji manju (maple leaf-shaped sweet cakes) from island stalls.
meals.dinner: Casual ramen or soba near Maruyama Park/Gion on return (~¥1,000–¥1,500 per person). Recommend Kyoto-style ramen at Shin-Puh-Kan food hall.

day_by_day.notes: This is the longest day of the trip — depart by 8:00 AM from Kyoto. A JR Pass (7-day) would cover Shinkansen and ferry costs and is highly recommended for this trip. The Peace Memorial Museum is appropriate for children aged 8+ with parental guidance; some exhibits are graphic. The floating torii is most dramatic at high tide — check tide tables in advance at miyajima-torii.jp.

day_by_day.morning: Golden Pavilion (Kinkakuji) & Ryoanji Temple — Take a bus or taxi to Kinkakuji (~¥500/adult, ~¥300/child), Kyoto's dazzling gold-leafed Zen temple reflected in a mirror pond — stunning in morning light. Walk 15 minutes to Ryoanji Temple (~¥600) to contemplate Japan's most famous rock garden, a UNESCO World Heritage Site. A wonderful moment of Zen calm for the whole family.
day_by_day.afternoon: Daitokuji Temple Complex & Zen Culture — Explore the vast Daitokuji compound, a collection of 24 sub-temples with beautiful moss gardens and Zen architecture. Many sub-temples are rarely visited by tourists. Participate in a zazen (Zen meditation) session if offered — some sub-temples welcome families for brief introductory sessions (~¥500–¥1,000).
day_by_day.evening: Traditional Kyoto Machiya Experience — Return to the Gion area and explore the preserved machiya (wooden townhouse) neighborhoods around your hotel. Visit the Gion Hatanaka area at dusk for atmospheric lantern-lit streets. End the evening with a relaxing onsen bath if your boutique hotel has one, or visit a nearby sento (public bath) for an authentic local experience (~¥500–¥800).

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at your hotel or a nearby café. Try a traditional Japanese breakfast set with grilled fish, miso soup, and pickled vegetables at a local restaurant (~¥800–¥1,200).
meals.lunch: Daitokuji Ikkyu — a historic restaurant near Daitokuji serving shojin ryori (Zen Buddhist vegetarian cuisine) in a serene garden setting. A unique cultural dining experience (~¥2,500–¥4,000 per person).
meals.dinner: Gion Nanba — a celebrated Kyoto restaurant serving seasonal kyo-kaiseki cuisine in a beautiful machiya setting. Order the mid-range set menu (~¥3,000–¥5,000 per person) for an authentic Kyoto fine dining experience.

day_by_day.notes: Kinkakuji is very crowded — arrive at opening (9:00 AM) to avoid peak crowds. Wednesday is a good day as some weekend visitors have left. Daitokuji's sub-temples have varying opening hours and some require advance booking for zazen — check individually. Bring cash as many smaller temples don't accept cards.

day_by_day.morning: Shinkansen to Tokyo — Check out of your Kyoto boutique hotel and take the Shinkansen Nozomi to Tokyo (~2 hrs 15 min, ~¥13,800 one way). Check into your Tokyo hotel (mid-range, Shinjuku or Shibuya area recommended for families). Drop luggage and head out to explore.
day_by_day.afternoon: Teamlab Borderless Digital Art Museum (Featured Experience) — Visit the newly reopened teamLab Borderless in Azabudai Hills, Tokyo (tickets ~¥3,200/adult, ~¥1,000/child ages 4–12, under 4 free — book online in advance, sells out quickly). Spend 2–3 hours immersed in boundaryless digital art installations where light, sound, and movement create a dreamlike interactive world. Absolutely magical for children and adults alike.
day_by_day.evening: Shibuya Crossing & Harajuku — Take the train to Shibuya and experience the world's busiest pedestrian crossing at rush hour — an iconic Tokyo spectacle. Walk to Harajuku's Takeshita Street for colorful street fashion, crepes, and candy floss. End the evening with dinner in Harajuku or Omotesando.

meals.breakfast: Quick breakfast at Kyoto Station's bakeries or coffee shops before boarding (~¥600–¥1,000). Enjoy the Shinkansen ride with an ekiben (station bento box) purchased at the platform.
meals.lunch: Ekiben on the Shinkansen — a beloved Japanese travel tradition. Choose from dozens of regional bento boxes at Kyoto Station (~¥1,200–¥2,000).
meals.dinner: Harajuku Gyoza Lou — a legendary gyoza restaurant near Harajuku Station serving crispy pan-fried dumplings with a cult following. Casual, cheap, and delicious (~¥800–¥1,200 per person). Queue expected but moves quickly.

day_by_day.notes: Book teamLab Borderless tickets weeks in advance — they sell out, especially on weekdays in April. The experience is timed entry. Luggage can be stored at Tokyo Station coin lockers while you explore if you check out of Kyoto early. Consider a Tokyo IC card top-up for seamless subway travel.

day_by_day.morning: Tsukiji Outer Market Food Tour (Featured Experience) — Head to Tsukiji Outer Market (the inner market moved to Toyosu, but the outer market remains vibrant). Join a guided food tour or self-explore the 400+ stalls selling fresh sushi, tamagoyaki, uni (sea urchin), crab claws, and Japanese street food. Arrive by 8:00 AM for the freshest experience. This is one of Tokyo's most exciting family food adventures.
day_by_day.afternoon: Ueno Park & Museums — Take the subway to Ueno, Tokyo's cultural hub. Visit Ueno Park, which may still have late cherry blossoms. Choose from world-class family-friendly museums: Tokyo National Museum (~¥1,000/adult, free for children under 18) for Japanese cultural artifacts, or the National Museum of Nature and Science (~¥630/adult, free for children) with dinosaur skeletons and space exhibits. Ueno Zoo (~¥600/adult, ~¥200/child) is also nearby for younger children.
day_by_day.evening: Akihabara Electric Town — Explore Tokyo's famous electronics and anime district. Browse multi-story electronics stores, anime merchandise shops, retro game arcades, and maid cafés. Try a round of arcade games at Taito Station or Club Sega — great family fun. Pick up unique Japanese electronics or character goods as souvenirs.

meals.breakfast: Tsukiji Outer Market feast — fresh sushi breakfast (maguro don or uni don) at one of the market's tiny sushi counters. A bucket-list experience (~¥1,500–¥3,000 per person).
meals.lunch: Ueno Yabu Soba — a historic soba restaurant near Ueno Park serving handmade buckwheat noodles since 1892. Classic Tokyo lunch experience (~¥1,000–¥1,800 per person).
meals.dinner: Akihabara ramen or tonkatsu — try Fuunji Tsukemen in the area for dipping ramen, or a family-friendly tonkatsu (breaded pork cutlet) restaurant (~¥1,200–¥2,000 per person).

day_by_day.notes: Tsukiji Outer Market is best visited on weekdays — Friday morning is ideal. Most stalls open by 5–6 AM and begin closing by noon. The Tokyo National Museum is closed on Mondays. Akihabara is most atmospheric in the evening when neon signs illuminate the streets. Keep children close in Akihabara's busy pedestrian zone.

day_by_day.morning: Senso-ji Temple & Asakusa District — Start the final day at Tokyo's oldest and most beloved temple, Senso-ji in Asakusa (free entry, open 24 hours). Walk through the iconic Kaminarimon Thunder Gate and the Nakamise shopping street lined with traditional craft shops and snack stalls. Draw an omikuji (fortune slip) for ~¥100 — a fun family tradition. Climb the nearby Tokyo Skytree (~¥2,100/adult, ~¥950/child for the lower deck at 350m) for spectacular final views of Tokyo.
day_by_day.afternoon: Odaiba Waterfront & teamLab Planets (Optional) — Take the futuristic Yurikamome driverless monorail to Odaiba, Tokyo's artificial island. Visit teamLab Planets (~¥3,200/adult, ~¥1,000/child — book online) for a different immersive art experience focused on water and garden installations, or explore DiverCity Tokyo Plaza for shopping and the giant Gundam statue. Alternatively, revisit any favorite Tokyo spots or do last-minute shopping in Shibuya 109 or Don Quijote.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell Dinner & Airport Transfer — Enjoy a final celebratory dinner in Tokyo before transferring to the airport. Depending on your departure flight, head to Narita (~60–90 min by Narita Express) or Haneda (~30 min by monorail) airport. Allow 3 hours before international departure.

meals.breakfast: Asakusa traditional breakfast — Nakamise street snacks (ningyo-yaki character cakes, senbei rice crackers) plus coffee from a nearby café (~¥600–¥1,000).
meals.lunch: Odaiba or Asakusa — try a conveyor belt sushi (kaiten-zushi) restaurant like Uobei or Sushiro for a fun, interactive, and affordable family lunch (~¥1,000–¥1,800 per person).
meals.dinner: Farewell splurge — Shabu-shabu (Japanese hot pot) at a mid-range restaurant in Shinjuku or near your hotel. Recommend Shabuzen or Nabezo for all-you-can-eat sets (~¥2,500–¥4,000 per person). A warm, communal, and memorable final meal.

day_by_day.notes: Tokyo Skytree tickets can be purchased on-site or online — weekends are busy, so arrive early (9:00 AM opening). Confirm your departure airport (Narita vs. Haneda) and allow ample transfer time. Consider shipping heavy souvenirs home via Yamato Transport's Takkyubin service from your hotel — reliable and affordable. Don't forget to use remaining IC card balance at airport convenience stores.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Japan Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

hotel.name: Maruyama Park, Gion district, Kyoto Boutique Stay

experiences.name: Cherry Blossom Viewing in Maruyama Park
experiences.description: Experience hanami (flower viewing) under Kyoto's most famous weeping cherry tree in Maruyama Park. Join locals for a traditional picnic beneath the blossoms, enjoy street food stalls selling sakura mochi and dango, and witness the magical illumination of the trees at night. A perfect family-friendly cultural experience that captures the essence of Japanese spring.

experiences.name: Teamlab Borderless Digital Art Museum
experiences.description: Immerse your family in a breathtaking world of interactive digital art installations spread across multiple rooms. Children and adults alike will be mesmerized by the flowing light displays, interactive projections, and immersive environments. This world-renowned museum blends technology and art in a uniquely Japanese way and is one of the most memorable family experiences in the country.

experiences.name: Tsukiji Outer Market Food Tour
experiences.description: Explore the vibrant Tsukiji Outer Market with your family and sample some of Japan's finest street food. Taste fresh sushi, tamagoyaki (sweet rolled omelette), grilled scallops, matcha ice cream, and more. Vendors are family-friendly and the lively atmosphere gives an authentic glimpse into Tokyo's culinary culture. A guided walking food tour can be arranged for deeper insight.

experiences.name: Arashiyama Bamboo Grove and Monkey Park
experiences.description: Walk through the iconic towering bamboo groves of Arashiyama and then hike up to the Iwatayama Monkey Park where over 120 wild Japanese macaques roam freely. Kids will love feeding the monkeys from inside a viewing hut while enjoying panoramic views of Kyoto below. Combine with a visit to nearby Tenryu-ji Temple garden for a full day of nature and culture.

experiences.name: Hiroshima Peace Memorial and Miyajima Island Day Trip
experiences.description: Take a meaningful and educational day trip from Kyoto or Osaka to Hiroshima's Peace Memorial Museum and Park, followed by a short ferry ride to Miyajima Island. See the iconic floating torii gate of Itsukushima Shrine, encounter friendly wild deer roaming freely, and enjoy local Hiroshima-style okonomiyaki for lunch. This culturally rich experience blends history, spirituality, and natural beauty in one unforgettable day.
experiences.location: Hiroshima Peace Park & Miyajima Island, Hiroshima Prefecture

day_by_day.morning: Arrival & Transfer — Flight LH lands at 13:00. No morning activities scheduled. Private luxury transfer (pre-booked limousine or Shinkansen Green Car) from the airport to Kyoto. Check-in at your Boutique Stay in Maruyama Park, Gion district.
day_by_day.afternoon: Gentle Gion Orientation Stroll — After settling in, take a leisurely walk through the historic Gion district. Explore the stone-paved Hanamikoji Street lined with traditional ochaya (teahouses), admire the preserved machiya townhouses, and soak in the atmosphere of old Kyoto. No rushed agenda — this is a soft landing into Japan.
day_by_day.evening: Cherry Blossom Viewing in Maruyama Park (Evening Illumination) — Step directly from your hotel into Maruyama Park to witness the iconic weeping cherry tree (shidarezakura) dramatically illuminated at night. The lantern-lit hanami experience is magical and exclusive to this brief spring window. Stroll the park paths with a warm sake or amazake in hand.

meals.breakfast: Meal on the aircraft or light snack at the airport lounge upon arrival.
meals.lunch: Kaiseki bento box or premium soba at a refined restaurant near Kyoto Station during your transfer layover — try Kyoto Cuisine Mizai or a station-level kaiseki counter.
meals.dinner: Kikunoi Honten (3 Michelin stars, 5-minute walk from Maruyama Park) — a landmark kaiseki restaurant offering a seasonal tasting menu showcasing spring ingredients like bamboo shoots, sakura-cured fish, and cherry blossom tofu. Reserve well in advance.

day_by_day.notes: Arrival day is intentionally light. Jet lag management is key — avoid overscheduling. Keep the evening walk short and calming. Confirm Kikunoi reservation before departure from home country. Private airport transfer should be pre-arranged with the hotel concierge.

day_by_day.morning: Cherry Blossom Viewing in Maruyama Park (Daytime Hanami) — Begin the morning with a full hanami experience in Maruyama Park. Arrive early to enjoy the park before crowds build. Spread a luxury picnic blanket beneath the great weeping cherry tree, enjoy seasonal sakura mochi and matcha prepared by your hotel, and photograph the blossoms in the soft morning light. The park is steps from your accommodation.
day_by_day.afternoon: Kiyomizudera Temple & Higashiyama Heritage Walk — Walk the ancient Higashiyama Sando stone-paved lanes to the UNESCO-listed Kiyomizudera Temple. Explore the wooden stage jutting over the hillside with panoramic views of cherry-blossomed Kyoto. Browse the artisan shops along Ninenzaka and Sannenzaka for premium ceramics, lacquerware, and textile souvenirs.
day_by_day.evening: Traditional Maiko Dinner Experience — Arrange a private ozashiki (geisha banquet) through your hotel concierge at a select Gion ochaya. Watch a maiko (apprentice geisha) perform traditional dances and play the shamisen while dining on an exquisite multi-course kaiseki meal. This is a once-in-a-lifetime cultural immersion exclusive to Kyoto.

meals.breakfast: In-hotel premium Japanese breakfast — grilled fish, dashi tamago, pickled vegetables, miso soup, and seasonal rice, served in the traditional ryokan style.
meals.lunch: Yudofu (tofu hot pot) lunch at Okutan Kiyomizu, a 350-year-old restaurant near Kiyomizudera, set in a serene garden. One of Kyoto's most authentic culinary traditions.
meals.dinner: Multi-course kaiseki dinner as part of the ozashiki maiko experience at a private Gion teahouse. Includes sake pairing and seasonal delicacies.

day_by_day.notes: The ozashiki experience requires advance booking — often weeks or months ahead. Your hotel concierge or a luxury travel agency (e.g., Artisans of Leisure) can facilitate this. Dress elegantly for the evening. Kiyomizudera is a 20-minute walk from the hotel through Higashiyama.

day_by_day.morning: Fushimi Inari Taisha Sunrise Hike — Depart early by private car (15-minute drive) to Fushimi Inari Shrine before the tourist crowds arrive. Hike through the iconic thousands of vermilion torii gates winding up the sacred mountain. The early morning mist, birdsong, and dappled light through the gates create an ethereal atmosphere. Hike as far as the family is comfortable — the lower loop (45 min) or the full summit (2–3 hrs).
day_by_day.afternoon: Nishiki Market & Pontocho Exploration — Return to central Kyoto and explore Nishiki Market, Kyoto's narrow 'Kitchen of Japan,' sampling premium street foods: fresh yuba (tofu skin), tsukemono pickles, grilled skewers, and matcha sweets. Afterward, stroll the atmospheric Pontocho alley running parallel to the Kamo River — a lantern-lit corridor of exclusive restaurants and bars.
day_by_day.evening: Kamo River Dinner — Dine at a premier Pontocho restaurant with kawayuka (riverside terrace dining) over the Kamo River. In spring, the cherry blossom trees lining the riverbanks may still be blooming, creating a breathtaking dinner backdrop.

meals.breakfast: Early light breakfast at the hotel before the sunrise hike — onigiri, miso soup, and green tea, or a packed breakfast prepared by the hotel.
meals.lunch: Gourmet street food tasting through Nishiki Market — curated self-guided tasting of premium bites including wagyu skewers, fresh tofu, and seasonal sweets.
meals.dinner: Mizai or Nakamura (one of Kyoto's oldest kaiseki restaurants, founded 1716) in Pontocho — seasonal kaiseki with kawayuka river terrace seating. Reserve the terrace table specifically.

day_by_day.notes: Arrive at Fushimi Inari by 6:00–6:30 AM for the best experience. Private car hire is recommended. Nishiki Market gets crowded by midday on weekends — plan accordingly. Kawayuka season typically runs May–September, so April terrace availability depends on the restaurant — confirm in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Arashiyama Bamboo Grove & Tenryuji Garden — Travel by private car (25 minutes) to Arashiyama. Walk through the towering bamboo grove in the early morning quiet. Visit the UNESCO World Heritage Tenryuji Temple with its stunning Sogenchi garden, where cherry blossoms reflect in the central pond — a scene of extraordinary beauty in April.
day_by_day.afternoon: Iwatayama Monkey Park — Hike up to the Iwatayama Monkey Park above Arashiyama for a family-favourite encounter with over 120 wild Japanese macaques. The panoramic views of Kyoto from the summit are spectacular. Afterward, enjoy a private boat ride along the Oi River (Hozu River) or a rickshaw ride through the Arashiyama village.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Gion — Relax at the hotel with an in-room sake tasting curated by the hotel sommelier, featuring premium Kyoto-region nihonshu varieties. Optional: evening walk through the quieter backstreets of Gion Shirakawa, where weeping cherry trees line the canal — one of Kyoto's most romantic nocturnal scenes.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast — full traditional Japanese spread with seasonal additions.
meals.lunch: Lunch at Shigetsu restaurant inside Tenryuji Temple — a refined shojin ryori (Buddhist vegetarian cuisine) meal in a tatami room overlooking the garden. One of Japan's most unique dining experiences.
meals.dinner: Private in-room kaiseki dinner arranged by the hotel, or dinner at Kichisen (3 Michelin stars) — widely considered one of Japan's greatest restaurants, requiring reservations months in advance.

day_by_day.notes: Arashiyama is most magical before 8:00 AM — aim to arrive early. The Monkey Park involves a 20-minute uphill hike — comfortable shoes required. Kichisen reservations are extremely exclusive; your hotel concierge or a luxury Japan travel specialist must assist. Shojin ryori at Shigetsu must be reserved in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Hiroshima Peace Memorial Museum & A-Bomb Dome — Day trip by Shinkansen (Green Car, 1 hour from Kyoto). Begin at the Hiroshima Peace Memorial Museum — a profoundly moving and historically essential experience for families. Walk through the Peace Memorial Park and stand before the iconic A-Bomb Dome. This is both educational and deeply humanizing for children and adults alike.
day_by_day.afternoon: Miyajima Island & Floating Torii Gate — Take the JR ferry to the sacred island of Miyajima. Marvel at the iconic 'floating' Otorii gate of Itsukushima Shrine rising from the Seto Inland Sea. Walk the island's forested paths, encounter friendly deer roaming freely, and climb (or take the ropeway) to Mt. Misen for panoramic views.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Kyoto — Shinkansen Green Car back to Kyoto. Relaxed dinner near the hotel to decompress after an emotionally and physically full day.

meals.breakfast: Early hotel breakfast before departing for Hiroshima.
meals.lunch: Hiroshima-style okonomiyaki (layered savoury pancake) at Okonomimura — a multi-storey building dedicated to Hiroshima's iconic dish. A fun, casual, and authentic family lunch experience.
meals.dinner: Warm, intimate dinner at Gion Nanba — a beloved Gion neighbourhood restaurant serving refined obanzai (Kyoto home-style cuisine) in a cosy machiya townhouse setting.

day_by_day.notes: The Peace Memorial Museum is recommended for children aged 8 and above. Prepare the family emotionally — it is a powerful experience. Allow at least 1.5 hours in the museum. The full Hiroshima + Miyajima day requires an early start (depart by 7:30 AM). Purchase Shinkansen Green Car tickets in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Nijo Castle & Kyoto Imperial Palace — Visit Nijo Castle, the opulent Edo-period shogun's residence with its famous 'nightingale floors' that chirp underfoot as a security measure. Explore the ornate painted sliding screens and stroll the castle's cherry-blossomed gardens. Then visit the nearby Kyoto Imperial Palace grounds, a serene expanse of traditional architecture and garden.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private Kimono Dressing & Tea Ceremony — Return to the Gion area for an exclusive private experience: professional kimono dressing in a historic machiya studio, followed by a private ura-senke or omotesenke school tea ceremony conducted by a certified tea master. Families can participate together — a deeply memorable cultural immersion.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset at Yasaka Pagoda & Gion Dinner — Walk to the iconic five-story Yasaka Pagoda in the Higashiyama hills for a golden-hour photo opportunity. Then enjoy dinner in the Gion district, still dressed in kimono if desired.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast.
meals.lunch: Bento lunch at a premium depachika (department store basement food hall) — Takashimaya or Isetan in Kyoto offer extraordinary artisanal bento boxes, wagyu sushi sets, and seasonal sweets. A fun family experience.
meals.dinner: Hyotei (3 Michelin stars, one of Japan's oldest restaurants, established 1837) — serving the legendary Kyoto-style kaiseki breakfast and dinner. Evening kaiseki featuring spring seasonal ingredients. Reserve months in advance.

day_by_day.notes: The private kimono and tea ceremony experience should be booked through a specialist operator (e.g., Maikoya or a private studio arranged by the hotel). Kimono rental includes professional dressing, hair styling, and photography. Children's kimono sizes are available. Hyotei is one of Japan's most storied restaurants — reservations are essential.

day_by_day.morning: Philosopher's Path & Nanzenji Temple — Walk the famous Philosopher's Path (Tetsugaku-no-michi), a stone-paved canal-side trail lined with hundreds of cherry trees (late bloomers may still be visible in mid-April). The 2km walk leads to Nanzenji Temple — one of Japan's most important Zen temples, featuring a grand sanmon gate, sub-temples with stunning rock gardens, and a charming 19th-century aqueduct.
day_by_day.afternoon: Teamlab Borderless Digital Art Museum — Travel to Osaka (30 min by Shinkansen or private car) for an afternoon at the Teamlab Borderless Digital Art Museum, one of the world's most extraordinary immersive art experiences. Families are utterly captivated — children and adults alike lose themselves in the luminous, interactive, boundary-dissolving digital installations. Book timed entry tickets well in advance.
day_by_day.evening: Osaka Dotonbori & Return — Experience the electric energy of Osaka's Dotonbori entertainment district — neon lights, giant mechanical crabs, and street food galore. Then return to Kyoto by Shinkansen for the night.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast.
meals.lunch: Lunch near Nanzenji — Okutan Nanzenji (sister restaurant to the Kiyomizudera location), serving yudofu tofu hot pot in a beautiful garden setting beside the temple.
meals.dinner: Osaka kushikatsu (deep-fried skewers) at Daruma Dotonbori — a fun, casual, family-friendly Osaka institution for a lively evening before returning to Kyoto. Alternatively, premium kappo cuisine at Kahala Osaka for a refined Osaka dining experience.

day_by_day.notes: Teamlab Borderless Osaka tickets sell out weeks in advance — book online before the trip. Wear comfortable, preferably dark-coloured clothing (light colours show projections beautifully but the environment is immersive). The Dotonbori evening is intentionally casual and energetic — a fun contrast to Kyoto's refinement.

day_by_day.morning: Kurama & Kibune Mountain Villages — Take a private car or the scenic Eizan Railway into the forested mountains north of Kyoto to the mystical village of Kurama. Hike the cedar-lined mountain trail through Kurama-dera Temple to the tranquil riverside village of Kibune — a 2-hour hike through ancient forest. This is Kyoto's wild, spiritual side, far from the tourist trail.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return & Nishijin Textile Workshop — Back in Kyoto, visit the Nishijin district for a private tour and demonstration at a traditional Nishijin-ori silk weaving atelier. Watch master weavers create the intricate brocade fabrics used in imperial court dress and high-end kimono. Commission a bespoke textile souvenir if desired.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell Gion Evening — Spend a final atmospheric evening in the Gion district. Stroll Shirakawa Canal, listen for the distant sound of shamisen from behind paper screens, and enjoy a nightcap of premium Japanese whisky at a sophisticated Gion bar.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast.
meals.lunch: Kibune kawadoko (river terrace) dining — in spring, some Kibune restaurants open their platforms suspended over the rushing Kibune River. Enjoy a refined kaiseki or somen noodle lunch above the crystal-clear mountain stream. Reserve in advance.
meals.dinner: Mizai or Nakamura — a return to one of Kyoto's finest for a celebratory final Kyoto dinner. Alternatively, a private in-room multi-course dinner arranged by the hotel for an intimate family evening.

day_by_day.notes: The Kurama-Kibune hike is approximately 2km and moderately steep — suitable for older children and adults. Wear hiking-appropriate footwear. The kawadoko river terrace at Kibune is one of Japan's most unique dining experiences — advance reservations are essential and fill quickly in spring. Kibune kawadoko season traditionally opens May 1, so April availability may be limited — confirm with the hotel concierge.

day_by_day.morning: Tsukiji Outer Market Food Tour (Tokyo Day Trip) — Travel to Tokyo by Shinkansen Green Car (2 hrs 15 min, depart early). Head directly to Tsukiji Outer Market for a guided premium food tour. Sample Japan's finest street foods: fresh uni (sea urchin), tamagoyaki (sweet rolled omelette), premium tuna sashimi, wagyu beef skewers, and seasonal seafood. A wonderful family culinary adventure.
day_by_day.afternoon: Teamlab Planets (Toyosu) or Odaiba Exploration — Visit Teamlab Planets in Toyosu — a more intimate, water-based Teamlab experience (different from Borderless) featuring extraordinary rooms of infinite flowers, mirrored water, and immersive light. Alternatively, explore the futuristic Odaiba waterfront district with its family-friendly attractions, teamLab, and views of Rainbow Bridge.
day_by_day.evening: Tokyo Luxury Hotel Overnight — Check in to a luxury Tokyo hotel (Park Hyatt Tokyo, Aman Tokyo, or The Peninsula Tokyo) for a one-night stay. Enjoy dinner with views of the Tokyo skyline.

meals.breakfast: Light hotel breakfast or Shinkansen bento (ekiben) — the premium bento boxes sold at Kyoto Station are a delightful Japanese travel tradition.
meals.lunch: Tsukiji Outer Market tasting tour — a curated selection of the market's finest offerings. No single restaurant — this is an immersive street food experience.
meals.dinner: New York Bar & Grill at Park Hyatt Tokyo (iconic Lost in Translation setting) — 52nd-floor panoramic Tokyo views with premium steaks, Japanese wagyu, and an extraordinary wine list. Alternatively, Sushi Saito (if reservations can be secured — one of Japan's most exclusive sushi counters) or Sukiyabashi Jiro Honten.

day_by_day.notes: Book Shinkansen Green Car tickets in advance. Tokyo luxury hotel must be pre-booked. Teamlab Planets tickets require advance online booking. The Tsukiji food tour is best with a private guide — arrange through the hotel concierge or a specialist operator. Sushi Saito reservations are nearly impossible without a Japanese connection — the hotel concierge of a top Tokyo hotel may be able to assist.

day_by_day.morning: Tokyo Highlights — Senso-ji Temple & Asakusa — Begin with a serene early morning visit to Senso-ji, Tokyo's oldest and most spectacular temple in the Asakusa district. The Nakamise shopping street leading to the temple offers premium traditional souvenirs: folding fans, lacquerware, ningyo dolls, and wagashi sweets. A beautiful, timeless Tokyo morning.
day_by_day.afternoon: Shibuya & Omotesando Luxury Shopping — Visit the iconic Shibuya Crossing — the world's busiest pedestrian intersection — then head to the elegant Omotesando boulevard for luxury shopping: flagship stores of Japanese designers (Issey Miyake, Comme des Garçons), premium concept stores (Dover Street Market), and the exquisite Omotesando Hills complex. Perfect for final souvenir and gift shopping.
day_by_day.evening: Departure Preparation & Farewell Dinner — Return to the hotel for final packing. Enjoy a farewell dinner at the hotel's signature restaurant or a nearby kaiseki counter. Transfer to Narita or Haneda airport for your departure flight.

meals.breakfast: Luxury hotel breakfast — full buffet or à la carte at the hotel's premium restaurant. Savour it — this is the final Japanese breakfast.
meals.lunch: Tempura Kondo (Ginza) — widely regarded as Tokyo's finest tempura restaurant, serving gossamer-light seasonal vegetable and seafood tempura in an intimate, refined setting. A perfect final lunch.
meals.dinner: Hotel signature restaurant farewell dinner, or Joël Robuchon Tokyo (if departing late) — the legendary French-Japanese fusion experience in the Garden Place Yebisu mansion. Alternatively, a premium sushi omakase counter in Ginza for a definitive final Japanese meal.

day_by_day.notes: Confirm departure flight time and plan airport transfer accordingly — allow 2.5–3 hours before international departure. Narita Express (N'EX) Green Car or private limousine transfer recommended. Duty-free shopping at the airport is excellent for final Japanese whisky, cosmetics, and confectionery purchases. Keep one carry-on bag accessible for any last-minute airport purchases.
